summary: Backend-only iteration 3. Verified new Anselma/Katsudoto additions: 'anselma-heritage' template in wedding category (4 wedding templates), enriched wedding default_config (hashtag, verse_text/ref, full names, parents, 3-chapter love_story, 2 events Akad+Resepsi, 1 bank, show_gift/show_wishes), rich-config PATCH persistence, public wishes POST/GET (success, validation 400s, invalid attending nulled, 404 on unknown slug, limit param, desc sort), owner-only /events/{id}/wishes (200 owner, 404 other user, 401 unauthenticated), plus public invitation payload exposing new config. Re-ran the 20-test regression suite: all pass after updating the template-count assertion (6 -> 7). Total 37/38 tests pass; the single failure is a genuine backend bug (wishes not cascade-deleted with the event).

minor.issue: Cascade deletes guests but NOT wishes (and not payments). Deleting an event leaves orphan documents in db.wishes forever. Add `await db.wishes.delete_many({'event_id': event_id})`.

config is $set wholesale, so a partial PATCH like {config:{bride_name:'x'}} wipes every other config key (love_story/events/banks/verse). Frontend EventEditor currently sends the full config so the UI works, but the API is data-loss prone. Recommend merging: $set {'config.<k>': v} per key or deep-merge with the stored config.
No pagination/offset and no rate limiting/spam protection on the public POST /wishes endpoint - anyone can flood the guestbook of any (even draft) event.
Accepts wishes for events with status='draft' (public GET /public/inv/{slug} returns 404 for drafts). Inconsistent: consider requiring published status.

action_items: Add wishes (and payments) cascade delete in DELETE /api/events/{event_id}
Make PATCH /api/events/{id} config merge instead of replace (or document replace-only contract)
Consider blocking wish submission on draft/unpublished events + basic rate limiting
critical_code_review_comments: server.py delete_event(): guests are cascade-deleted but wishes are not - orphan data grows.
server.py update_event(): `$set {'config': cfg}` replaces the entire nested config; the enriched wedding config (love_story/events/banks) makes this materially riskier than before.
server.py is 744 lines and approaching the 700-line split threshold - consider splitting routers (auth/events/public/payments) into modules.
Wishes have no owner moderation/delete endpoint - a public guestbook without delete/hide is an abuse vector.
seed_data_creation: Two MongoDB-seeded test users + sessions (deleted in teardown), TEST_ prefixed wedding events and wishes (deleted in teardown; verified 0 leftover TEST wishes). One pre-existing test.user.* doc from a prior iteration remains in db.users.
test_credentials: No passwords - Mongo-seeded session_token used via Authorization: Bearer (see /app/memory/test_credentials.md)
context_for_next_testing_agent: Suite = /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py (20 tests, template count now asserts 7) + /app/backend/tests/test_wishes_and_config.py (18 tests, new features). Run: cd /app/backend && python -m pytest tests/ -v. Only test_delete_event_removes_wishes fails (real cascade bug). test_patch_rich_config_persists intentionally asserts replace-semantics ('verse_ref' not in config) - flip it if the main agent implements config merging. Frontend of the new Katsudoto-style public invitation (cover gate, timeline, countdown, gift copy button, wishes form) has NOT been UI-tested yet.
rca_of_the_issue: DELETE /api/events/{event_id} only issues db.guests.delete_many; the new db.wishes collection was added without extending the cascade. PATCH data-loss stems from `$set {'config': payload.config}` treating config as an opaque blob.
